note: Kulp's commentary on 1:1 quotes the oath wording two ways ('not less' and 'not more' than half); no oath wording is drawn. Briefs for 1:6 rest on the mishnah text alone (no Kulp explanation available).

briefs.teaching: Two people grip a cloak, each claiming it (or one claims all and the other half): each swears, and they split it half and half; or three quarters and one quarter.

scenes.a: Both claim all: two men grip opposite ends of a plain cloak in a market street, each pulling and pointing at himself. Outcome box: the cloak shown cut into two EQUAL halves.
scenes.b: One claims all, one claims half: one man holds his arms wide, the other holds one hand flat as if showing half. Outcome box: the cloak cut into two UNEQUAL pieces, one three times as large as the other.

briefs.badge_later: none (the outcome box shows the split; fractions are overlay text, not drawn)
briefs.avoid: Oath wording (Kulp quotes it two ways); any violence; text on the cloak.

briefs.teaching: Two men on one animal, both saying it is all theirs: each swears and they split it. If they later agree, or there are witnesses, they split without an oath.

scenes.main: On a dirt road, a donkey with one man sitting on it and a second man walking beside holding its rope; both point at themselves and look indignant.
scenes.left_box: Both men with a raised right hand (swearing) and the donkey's value shown as two equal heaps of gold coins.
scenes.right_box: The two men shaking hands, a third man (a witness) standing between them, and the same two equal heaps of coins.

briefs.teaching: A rider sees a lost object and tells his friend 'give it to me'; the friend picks it up and says 'I acquired it': he keeps it. If he first gave it to the rider and then said 'I got it first', his claim means nothing.

scenes.a: A man sits on a donkey pointing down at a leather purse on the road; his friend, on foot, picks it up and hugs it to his chest with a triumphant grin while the rider looks surprised. Badge later: KEEPS on the friend.
scenes.b: The same road: the friend has handed the purse up to the rider, who holds it; the friend now points to himself, clearly too late, while the rider holds the purse firmly. Badge later: NO-CLAIM on the friend.

briefs.avoid: Making either man look dishonest; the mishnah says only that he said he acquired it.

briefs.teaching: If a man says 'my field acquires it' while others chase a lost deer with a broken leg or pigeons that cannot fly, he acquires it. If the deer runs freely or the pigeons fly, what he said means nothing.

scenes.a: A field: a deer with a bandaged, clearly broken front leg limps along; two men run toward it from the far side; the field's owner stands in the middle with a hand on his chest, declaring. A fence encloses the field. Badge later: KEEPS on the owner.
scenes.b: The same field: a healthy deer bounds across it toward the open gate, pigeons flying above, the same two men chasing; the owner stands with a hand on his chest. Badge later: NO-CLAIM on the owner.

briefs.avoid: Cruelty to animals; showing the deer's injury graphically (a neat bandage only).

briefs.teaching: What a man's minor children, Canaanite slaves and wife find belongs to him; what his adult children, Hebrew slaves and divorced wife find belongs to them.

scenes.main: A household: a father at a table smiling; a small child hands him a found purse.
scenes.left_box: A small child giving a purse to the father, the father keeping it.
scenes.right_box: A grown daughter holding a purse of her own, the father looking on.

briefs.svg: Matrix: found by minor son or daughter; Canaanite slave; wife; adult son or daughter; Hebrew slave; divorced wife. Column: whose it is.
briefs.badge_later: KEEPS (new): father in the left box, the finder in the right box
briefs.avoid: Implying slavery is approved; the SVG states the mishnah's rule neutrally.

briefs.teaching: Found debt documents: if they record a lien on the debtor's property, do not return them, since the court would collect from the property. If there is no lien, Rabbi Meir says he may return them; the Sages say not to return them in either case.
briefs.svg: Matrix: columns 'With a lien on property' and 'Without a lien'; rows 'Rabbi Meir' and 'The Sages'. Cells: 'Do not return' or 'Return it', drawn with two small icons (a curved return arrow; a stop hand).
briefs.badge_later: RETURN / DO-NOT-RETURN icons (drawn inside the SVG)
briefs.avoid: Stating the reason beyond what Kulp says (the mishnah's reason: the court could collect from the property).
briefs.source: Mishnah 1:6 text only (Sefaria has no Kulp explanation for 1:6, only his questions)

briefs.teaching: Found bills of divorce, writs of emancipation, wills, deeds of gift and receipts are not returned, since the writer may have written them and then changed his mind.

scenes.main: A man standing on a path holding up a rolled document he found, looking uncertain; Badge later: DO-NOT-RETURN near him.
scenes.left_box: The document was lost after being given: a woman receives it from a man's hand and later loses it.
scenes.right_box: The writer wrote it, changed his mind and set it aside: a man at a desk pushing the document away, shaking his head; it falls to the ground.

briefs.avoid: Specifying the document type in the picture; implying the finder is at fault.

briefs.teaching: Documents that must be returned (court documents, a satchel or bundle of three, three documents with one borrower or one lender per Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel), the document of unknown type that waits until Elijah comes, and postscripts.
briefs.svg: List with sprite figures: court documents -> return; found in a satchel or a bundle of three tied together -> return; three documents where one man borrowed from three -> to the borrower; one man lent to three -> to the lender; a document of unknown nature among his own -> keep until Elijah comes; postscript -> follow it.
briefs.badge_later: RETURN icon drawn inside the SVG
